title: Pragmatics-Preserving MT Benchmark Item
description: Schema for a single benchmark item in the Pragmatics-Preserving Machine Translation for Indian Dialogue benchmark. Schema version 0.1.0. See benchmark/schema/annotation_schema.md for field-by-field documentation.

dialogueTurn.description: A single dialogue turn, used for both context turns and the source utterance.

turn_id.description: 1-based position of this turn within the item's dialogue.

speaker_id.description: Short anonymous speaker label, e.g. 'A' or 'B'. Never a real name.

speaker_role.description: Social role of the speaker, e.g. 'Student', 'Manager', 'Younger sibling'.

text.description: The utterance text in romanized Hindi or Hinglish.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of the item schema this item conforms to.

item_id.description: Unique item identifier: {HIN|HNG}_{POL|IND|STA|CSW}_{NNN}. HIN=Hindi, HNG=Hinglish. POL=politeness/formality, IND=indirect request/refusal, STA=stance/emotion, CSW=code-switching.

language.description: Language of the source utterance. Hindi and Hinglish are distinct values.

language_variety.description: Free-text variety description, e.g. 'Standard Hindi (romanized)' or 'Urban Hinglish (code-mixed)'.

translation_direction.description: Source-target direction. Must agree with the language field.

source_type.description: How the item was produced. NATURAL and ADAPTED require a documented source_reference.

source_reference.description: Provenance for NATURAL or ADAPTED items. Must be null when provenance cannot be documented.

license.description: Licensing status of the source material. Use 'TO_BE_CONFIRMED' until licensing is verified.

review_status.description: Human review state. Only a native speaker may move an item to APPROVED.

context.description: Zero to three previous dialogue turns. Zero turns is allowed only for context-independent items.

source_utterance.description: The utterance to be translated. Its text must be non-empty.

literal_gloss.description: A close, deliberately flat English gloss of the source utterance, for non-speakers of the source language.

listener_role.description: Social role of the addressee of the source utterance.

relationship.description: Type of social relationship between speaker and listener. Specific roles live in speaker_role and listener_role.

relative_status.description: Social status of the speaker relative to the listener.

familiarity.description: How well the speaker and listener know each other.

primary_phenomenon.description: The single pragmatic category this item is built to test. Must agree with the item_id category code.

secondary_phenomena.description: Additional pragmatic dimensions that are also at stake. May be empty.

speech_act.description: The intended communicative function of the source utterance.

politeness_level.description: Ordinal degree of respect/deference encoded in the utterance.

formality_level.description: Register of the utterance. Kept separate from politeness.

stance.description: The speaker's attitude toward the listener, proposition, or situation.

emotion.description: The affective state expressed by the speaker.

indirectness.description: Whether the utterance communicates its intent explicitly or through implication.

code_switch_function.description: Discourse function of a language switch. Use NOT_APPLICABLE or null when the switch carries no pragmatic load.

context_required.description: True when the utterance cannot be correctly interpreted without the context turns.

context_status.description: Three-way judgment of how much the context matters for interpretation.

minimum_context_window.description: Smallest number of previous turns needed for a correct reading. Must not exceed the number of context turns.

relevant_context_turns.description: turn_id values of the context turns that carry the disambiguating information. Required to be non-empty when context_status is REQUIRED.

context_explanation.description: Short prose explanation of what the context contributes. May be empty for NOT_REQUIRED items.

preservation_requirement.description: Plain statement of what an acceptable translation must preserve.

reference_translations.description: One or more pragmatically acceptable English translations.

acceptable_variants.description: Further translations judged acceptable, recorded separately from the primary references. May be empty.

contrastive_translation.description: A semantically close but pragmatically wrong translation, minimally different from the reference.

contrastive_error.description: Explanation of exactly what pragmatic meaning the contrastive translation breaks.

contrastive_error_category.description: The single pragmatic dimension the contrastive translation breaks.

severity.description: How damaging the contrastive error is. See benchmark/schema/severity_guidelines.md.

creator_notes.description: Notes from whoever drafted the item, including known uncertainties.

annotator_notes.description: Notes added during annotation. Empty until an annotator fills it in.

annotator_ids.description: Pseudonymous annotator identifiers. Empty until the item is annotated. Never real personal information.

adjudicator_id.description: Pseudonymous adjudicator identifier, or null when no adjudication has happened.

agreement_status.description: State of inter-annotator agreement for this item.

annotation_version.description: Version counter for the annotation record on this item.

allOf.$comment: When context is REQUIRED, the item must actually carry context turns and name which ones matter.
Context-independent items must not claim a required context window.
Code-switching items must name a real discourse function for the switch.
NATURAL and ADAPTED items require documented provenance.
